beginner.summary: For aspiring penetration testers, security analysts and sysadmins who can use a Linux shell and understand TCP/IP but have not run a structured, authorised test. It teaches the full workflow against isolated, learner-owned labs (HTB/TryHackMe-style ranges, Metasploitable and DVWA): legal authorisation and rules of engagement first, then PTES, OSSTMM and NIST SP 800-115 methodology, reconnaissance, Nmap scanning, vulnerability analysis with CVSS 4.0, web testing with Burp Suite, exploitation with Metasploit, Linux and Windows privilege escalation, password auditing, pivoting, wireless awareness, and remediation-focused reporting with a defence and detection angle throughout.
prerequisites: Comfortable on a Linux shell: navigating directories, editing files, piping commands and managing packages with apt
Understands TCP/IP basics: IP addressing, ports, the TCP handshake, DNS and HTTP request/response
Owns an isolated practice lab (nested VMs or a private HTB/TryHackMe range) with legal authorisation to attack every target in it
outcomes: Scope an authorised test, record rules of engagement and map activity to PTES, OSSTMM and NIST SP 800-115
Run a full reconnaissance-to-exploitation workflow against lab targets using Nmap, Burp Suite and Metasploit
Escalate privileges on Linux and Windows lab hosts and audit passwords with Hashcat and John the Ripper
Score findings with CVSS 4.0, write a remediation-focused report and describe the defensive detections each attack leaves behind
